Exercise 3: create intraday returns¶

In [9]:
# Split the xts object by days
msft_split <- split(msft_xts, f = "days")
# Apply makeReturns to each day individually to avoid overnight returns
msft_ret_list <- lapply(msft_split, makeReturns)
# Bind the list back into a single xts object
msft_intraday_returns <- do.call(rbind, msft_ret_list)

# 2. BAC Intraday Returns
bac_split <- split(bac_xts, f = "days")
bac_ret_list <- lapply(bac_split, makeReturns)
bac_intraday_returns <- do.call(rbind, bac_ret_list)

# 3. XOM Intraday Returns
xom_split <- split(xom_xts, f = "days")
xom_ret_list <- lapply(xom_split, makeReturns)
xom_intraday_returns <- do.call(rbind, xom_ret_list)

Exercise 4: create and compare RV created from prices and returns¶

In [10]:
#calculate RV from prices with makeReturns=TRUE
RV_msft <- rCov(rData = msft_xts, makeReturns = TRUE)
index(RV_msft) <- as.Date(index(RV_msft))
RV_bac <- rCov(rData = bac_xts, makeReturns = TRUE)
index(RV_bac) <- as.Date(index(RV_bac))
RV_xom <- rCov(rData = xom_xts, makeReturns = TRUE)
index(RV_xom) <- as.Date(index(RV_xom))

#calculate RV from returns with makeReturns=FALSE
RV_msft_ret <- rCov(rData = msft_intraday_returns, makeReturns = FALSE)
index(RV_msft_ret) <- as.Date(index(RV_msft_ret))
RV_bac_ret <- rCov(rData = bac_intraday_returns, makeReturns = FALSE)
index(RV_bac_ret) <- as.Date(index(RV_bac_ret))
RV_xom_ret <- rCov(rData = xom_intraday_returns, makeReturns = FALSE)
index(RV_xom_ret) <- as.Date(index(RV_xom_ret))
In [11]:
# 1. MSFT Comparison
# Calculate the difference between the two RV series
diff_msft <- RV_msft - RV_msft_ret
# Calculate avg, min, and max differences (handling any potential NAs)
msft_avg <- mean(diff_msft, na.rm = TRUE)
msft_min <- min(diff_msft, na.rm = TRUE)
msft_max <- max(diff_msft, na.rm = TRUE)
# Print the results
cat("MSFT RV Differences -> Avg:", msft_avg, " | Min:", msft_min, " | Max:", msft_max, "\n")

# 2. BAC Comparison
diff_bac <- RV_bac - RV_bac_ret
bac_avg <- mean(diff_bac, na.rm = TRUE)
bac_min <- min(diff_bac, na.rm = TRUE)
bac_max <- max(diff_bac, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("BAC RV Differences  -> Avg:", bac_avg, " | Min:", bac_min, " | Max:", bac_max, "\n")

# 3. XOM Comparison
diff_xom <- RV_xom - RV_xom_ret
xom_avg <- mean(diff_xom, na.rm = TRUE)
xom_min <- min(diff_xom, na.rm = TRUE)
xom_max <- max(diff_xom, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("XOM RV Differences  -> Avg:", xom_avg, " | Min:", xom_min, " | Max:", xom_max, "\n")

Exercise 5: compare intraday RVs for periods¶

In [12]:
# Define the time intervals and their labels for the legend
intervals <- c("T07:00/T09:29", "T09:30/T10:59", "T11:00/T14:29", "T14:30/T15:59", "T16:00/T18:00")
labels <- c("7:00-9:29", "9:30-10:59", "11:00-14:29", "14:30-15:59", "16:00-18:00")
plot_colors <- c("black", "gray30", "gray50", "gray70", "gray85")
In [13]:
# 1. MSFT Sub-period RV
msft_rv_1 <- rCov(rData = msft_intraday_returns[intervals[1]], makeReturns = FALSE)
msft_rv_2 <- rCov(rData = msft_intraday_returns[intervals[2]], makeReturns = FALSE)
msft_rv_3 <- rCov(rData = msft_intraday_returns[intervals[3]], makeReturns = FALSE)
msft_rv_4 <- rCov(rData = msft_intraday_returns[intervals[4]], makeReturns = FALSE)
msft_rv_5 <- rCov(rData = msft_intraday_returns[intervals[5]], makeReturns = FALSE)

# Combine and fix index
msft_sub_rv <- cbind(msft_rv_1, msft_rv_2, msft_rv_3, msft_rv_4, msft_rv_5)
index(msft_sub_rv) <- as.Date(index(msft_sub_rv))
colnames(msft_sub_rv) <- labels


# Calculate the TOTAL sum of RV across all days for each sub-period
msft_sum_rv <- colSums(msft_sub_rv, na.rm = TRUE)
options(repr.plot.width = 14, repr.plot.height = 7)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(7, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
# Plot 1: Total Sum Line Plot
plot(msft_sum_rv, type = "b", col = "red", pch = 16, xaxt = "n", 
     xlab = "", ylab = "Total Sum Realized Variance", 
     main = "MSFT - Intraday Volatility (Total)")
axis(1, at = 1:5, labels = labels, las = 2) # las = 2 makes labels vertical

# Plot 2: Boxplot Distribution
boxplot(as.data.frame(msft_sub_rv), names = labels, las = 2, 
        ylab = "Daily Realized Variance", main = "MSFT - Daily RV Distribution")
cat("\n--- MSFT Mean RV by Sub-period ---\n")
print(colMeans(msft_sub_rv, na.rm = TRUE))

--- MSFT Mean RV by Sub-period ---
   7:00-9:29   9:30-10:59  11:00-14:29  14:30-15:59  16:00-18:00 
7.761139e-05 6.558249e-05 5.355973e-05 3.168965e-05 2.207521e-04

The plotted Realized Variance for MSFT demonstrates a distinct intraday volatility pattern, giving us a U or V shape, heavily skewed toward the market close. Volatility begins relatively high in the morning, drops significantly during the mid-day hours (11:00-15:59) as trading activity subsides, and experiences a massive surge between 16:00 and 18:00. Furthermore, the daily RV distribution boxplots reveal that this late-day spike is driven by extreme variance outliers, likely caused by closing auctions, institutional rebalancing, and post-market news events. Consequently, the data clearly identifies the period surrounding the daily close as the most volatile and risk-prone segment of the trading day.

--- BAC Mean RV by Sub-period ---
   7:00-9:29   9:30-10:59  11:00-14:29  14:30-15:59  16:00-18:00 
0.0001495171 0.0001234494 0.0001130947 0.0000528366 0.0001841342

Bank of America exhibits a prominent U-shaped volatility pattern, with realized variance starting high in the morning, dipping to a low in the mid-afternoon (14:30-15:59), and sharply spiking into the market close. While the late-day period (16:00-18:00) displays the highest total and average volatility, the daily distribution boxplots reveal a crucial difference in how that volatility is distributed. Specifically, the pre-market/early morning session (7:00-9:29) contains a singular, massive volatility outlier, likely triggered by a major pre-market earnings report or macroeconomic data release. Consequently, while the end-of-day trading is consistently the most volatile on average, the pre-market is similarly volatile, althought mainly driven by one huge outlier.

   7:00-9:29   9:30-10:59  11:00-14:29  14:30-15:59  16:00-18:00 
3.700015e-04 6.486603e-05 4.737451e-05 2.890006e-05 1.090225e-04

Unlike the previous assets, ExxonMobil exhibits a heavily skewed morning volatility pattern, with the highest total and mean realized variance occurring in the earliest trading session (7:00-9:29). After the initial morning surge, volatility drops sharply and reaches its lowest point mid-afternoon (14:30-15:59) before experiencing a milder, typical uptick towards the market close. The daily distribution boxplot reveals that this massive morning variance is driven by at least one extraordinary outlier that completely dwarfs the activity seen in any other period.

Exercise 6: compare intraday sub RVs sums with daily RV¶

In [16]:
# 1. MSFT Difference
msft_rv_daily <- rCov(na.omit(msft_intraday_returns["T07:00/T18:00"]), makeReturns = FALSE)
index(msft_rv_daily) <- as.Date(index(msft_rv_daily))
colnames(msft_rv_daily) <- "Full_RV"

msft_combined <- msft_rv_daily
for (i in seq_along(intervals)) {
  sub_ret      <- na.omit(msft_intraday_returns[intervals[i]])
  daily_sub_rv <- rCov(sub_ret, makeReturns = FALSE)
  index(daily_sub_rv) <- as.Date(index(daily_sub_rv))
  colnames(daily_sub_rv) <- paste0("P", i)
  msft_combined <- merge(msft_combined, daily_sub_rv, join = "left")
}

msft_combined[is.na(msft_combined)] <- 0

msft_rv_summed <- rowSums(msft_combined[, 2:6])
msft_rv_diff   <- msft_combined[, 1] - msft_rv_summed

plot.zoo(msft_rv_diff, col = "darkgreen", xlab = "", ylab = "Difference",
         main = "MSFT: Full RV vs. Summed RV")

cat(sprintf("\n--- MSFT Additivity Summary ---\n"))
cat(sprintf("Mean Difference: %e\n", mean(msft_rv_diff, na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Max Difference : %e\n", max(msft_rv_diff,  na.rm = TRUE)))
cat(sprintf("Min Difference : %e\n", min(msft_rv_diff,  na.rm = TRUE)))

--- MSFT Additivity Summary ---
Mean Difference: 2.881034e-21
Max Difference : 8.673617e-19
Min Difference : -8.673617e-19

Exercise 7: shares of intraday sub RVs on total RV¶

In [31]:
# 1. MSFT Percentage Share
# Use as.numeric() on the denominator to fix array mismatch
msft_pct <- (msft_combined[, 2:6] / as.numeric(msft_combined[, 1])) * 100

# Handle any potential division by zero
msft_pct[is.na(msft_pct) | msft_pct == Inf] <- 0
colnames(msft_pct) <- labels

msft_avg_pct <- colMeans(msft_pct, na.rm = TRUE)


barplot(msft_avg_pct, col = plot_colors, las = 2, ylab = "Average % Share",
        main = "MSFT: Avg Intraday Share")
In [30]:
# 2. BAC Percentage Share
bac_pct <- (bac_combined[, 2:6] / as.numeric(bac_combined[, 1])) * 100

bac_pct[is.na(bac_pct) | bac_pct == Inf] <- 0
colnames(bac_pct) <- labels

bac_avg_pct <- colMeans(bac_pct, na.rm = TRUE)


barplot(bac_avg_pct, col = plot_colors, las = 2, ylab = "Average % Share",
        main = "BAC: Avg Intraday Share")
In [29]:
# 3. XOM Percentage Share
xom_pct <- (xom_combined[, 2:6] / as.numeric(xom_combined[, 1])) * 100

xom_pct[is.na(xom_pct) | xom_pct == Inf] <- 0
colnames(xom_pct) <- labels

xom_avg_pct <- colMeans(xom_pct, na.rm = TRUE)


barplot(xom_avg_pct, col = plot_colors, las = 2, ylab = "Average % Share",
        main = "XOM: Avg Intraday Share")

MSFT: The late-day and post-market window (16:00-18:00) heavily dominates, capturing over 30% of the average daily variance.

BAC: Volatility is highly concentrated during the regular morning trading session (9:30-10:59), which accounts for nearly 28% of the daily total.

XOM: The pre-market period (7:00-9:29) holds the highest share of variance (roughly 28%).

While standard trading hours (9:30 - 16:00) are undeniably important, our findings prove that extended hours are just as critical. Depending on the asset class and its specific news cycle (like overnight oil prices for XOM or post-market tech earnings for MSFT), pre-market and post-market sessions frequently generate the largest share of a stock's total daily volatility.

Exercise 8: repeat with prices instead of returns¶

In [22]:
# Helper function to safely calculate sub-period RV- we were encountering problem with too few values in some intervals to calculate the returns
safe_rv <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) > 1) {
    xts(as.numeric(rCov(x, makeReturns = TRUE)), order.by = as.Date(index(x)[1]))
  } else if (nrow(x) == 1) {
    xts(0, order.by = as.Date(index(x)[1]))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
}
# 1. MSFT Prices (Using pre-calculated RV_msft)
msft_combined_pr <- RV_msft
colnames(msft_combined_pr) <- "Full_RV"

for (i in seq_along(intervals)) {
  sub_split <- split(na.omit(msft_xts[intervals[i]]), f = "days")
  daily_sub_rv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sub_split, safe_rv))
  colnames(daily_sub_rv) <- paste0("P", i)
  msft_combined_pr <- merge(msft_combined_pr, daily_sub_rv, join = "left")
}
msft_combined_pr[is.na(msft_combined_pr)] <- 0

# 2. BAC Prices (Using pre-calculated RV_bac)
bac_combined_pr <- RV_bac
colnames(bac_combined_pr) <- "Full_RV"

for (i in seq_along(intervals)) {
  sub_split <- split(na.omit(bac_xts[intervals[i]]), f = "days")
  daily_sub_rv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sub_split, safe_rv))
  colnames(daily_sub_rv) <- paste0("P", i)
  bac_combined_pr <- merge(bac_combined_pr, daily_sub_rv, join = "left")
}
bac_combined_pr[is.na(bac_combined_pr)] <- 0


# 3. XOM Prices (Using pre-calculated RV_xom)
xom_combined_pr <- RV_xom
colnames(xom_combined_pr) <- "Full_RV"

for (i in seq_along(intervals)) {
  sub_split <- split(na.omit(xom_xts[intervals[i]]), f = "days")
  daily_sub_rv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sub_split, safe_rv))
  colnames(daily_sub_rv) <- paste0("P", i)
  xom_combined_pr <- merge(xom_combined_pr, daily_sub_rv, join = "left")
}
xom_combined_pr[is.na(xom_combined_pr)] <- 0

8.6: Additivity¶

Now, the differences seem not to be due to the number of digits R can pass. While the differences between daily RV and the sum of intraday RV was tiny (around $10^{-20}$) and took on positive and negative values, the differences here are much larger, and almost purely non-negative. The differences are still small, but using prices yields much much larger differences of up to e-05. The difference is driven entirely by missing boundary returns (gap variance). Because we slice the price series into isolated chunks, the price jumps that occur exactly between the defined intervals (e.g., the return from 9:29 to 9:30, or 10:59 to 11:00) are completely lost, resulting in larger, non-negative differences.

# 1. MSFT 
BV_msft <- rBPCov(rData = msft_xts, makeReturns = TRUE)
index(BV_msft) <- as.Date(index(BV_msft))

MedRV_msft <- rMedRVar(rData = msft_xts, makeReturns = TRUE)

# Graphical Comparison
plot.zoo(cbind(RV_msft, BV_msft, MedRV_msft), screens = 1, col = c("black", "red", "blue"),
         main = "MSFT: RV vs BPV vs MedRV", ylab = "Variance")
legend("topright", legend = c("RV", "BPV", "MedRV"), col = c("black", "red", "blue"), lty = 1, cex = 0.8)

# Seminar Jump Logic
j_medRV_msft <- RV_msft - MedRV_msft
jumps_test_medRV_msft <- BNSjumpTest(msft_xts, IVestimator = "rMedRVar", IQestimator = "rMedRQuar", makeReturns = TRUE) 

TT_msft <- nrow(jumps_test_medRV_msft)
I_medRV_msft <- sapply(1:TT_msft, function(j) {
  # Adding a safe check in case a day failed to calculate and returned NA
  if (!is.na(jumps_test_medRV_msft[j, "p.value"]) && jumps_test_medRV_msft[j, "p.value"] < 0.05) { 1 } else { 0 }
})

# Isolate only the statistically significant jumps
J_medRV_msft <- j_medRV_msft * I_medRV_msft

Exercise 10: compare sqrt(RV) with GARCH¶

In [41]:
# Extract the last price of each day using endpoints
msft_daily_prices <- msft_xts[endpoints(msft_xts, on = "days")]
bac_daily_prices  <- bac_xts[endpoints(bac_xts, on = "days")]
xom_daily_prices  <- xom_xts[endpoints(xom_xts, on = "days")]

# Calculate daily log returns
msft_daily_ret <- na.omit(diff(log(msft_daily_prices)))
bac_daily_ret  <- na.omit(diff(log(bac_daily_prices)))
xom_daily_ret  <- na.omit(diff(log(xom_daily_prices)))

# Standardize index to Date format to match RV indices perfectly
index(msft_daily_ret) <- as.Date(index(msft_daily_ret))
index(bac_daily_ret)  <- as.Date(index(bac_daily_ret))
index(xom_daily_ret)  <- as.Date(index(xom_daily_ret))

# 2. Specify the ARMA(0,0)-GARCH(1,1) Model
garch_spec <- ugarchspec(
  variance.model = list(model = "sGARCH", garchOrder = c(1, 1)),
  mean.model = list(armaOrder = c(0, 0), include.mean = TRUE),
  distribution.model = "norm"
)

# 3. Fit Models and Extract Conditional Volatility
# MSFT
msft_garch_fit <- ugarchfit(spec = garch_spec, data = msft_daily_ret)
msft_sigma <- xts(sigma(msft_garch_fit), order.by = index(msft_daily_ret))

# BAC
bac_garch_fit <- ugarchfit(spec = garch_spec, data = bac_daily_ret)
bac_sigma <- xts(sigma(bac_garch_fit), order.by = index(bac_daily_ret))

# XOM
xom_garch_fit <- ugarchfit(spec = garch_spec, data = xom_daily_ret)
xom_sigma <- xts(sigma(xom_garch_fit), order.by = index(xom_daily_ret))

# 4. Merge GARCH Sigma with Realized Volatility (sqrt(RV))
msft_comp <- merge(msft_sigma, sqrt(RV_msft), join = "inner")
colnames(msft_comp) <- c("GARCH", "Realized")

bac_comp <- merge(bac_sigma, sqrt(RV_bac), join = "inner")
colnames(bac_comp) <- c("GARCH", "Realized")

xom_comp <- merge(xom_sigma, sqrt(RV_xom), join = "inner")
colnames(xom_comp) <- c("GARCH", "Realized")

# 5. Graphical Comparison

par(mfrow = c(3, 1), mar = c(3, 4, 3, 2))

plot.zoo(msft_comp, screens = 1, col = c("red", "black"), 
         main = "MSFT: GARCH vs Realized Volatility", ylab = "Volatility")
legend("topleft", legend = c("GARCH(1,1)", "Realized Volatility"), col = c("red", "black"), lty = 1, cex = 0.8)

plot.zoo(bac_comp, screens = 1, col = c("red", "black"), 
         main = "BAC: GARCH vs Realized Volatility", ylab = "Volatility")
legend("topleft", legend = c("GARCH(1,1)", "Realized Volatility"), col = c("red", "black"), lty = 1, cex = 0.8)

plot.zoo(xom_comp, screens = 1, col = c("red", "black"), 
         main = "XOM: GARCH vs Realized Volatility", ylab = "Volatility")
legend("topleft", legend = c("GARCH(1,1)", "Realized Volatility"), col = c("red", "black"), lty = 1, cex = 0.8)

The estimates illustrated above show the fundamental difference between RV using high frequency data and GARCH models volatility. Grach is much more smooth and cannot capture the changes as fast as the RV. Garc is not capturing spikes or sudden flusctuations, it is showing some trend that is clearly lagged. With more data there is more fluctuations and threfore the garch is less smooth (msft), but that doesnt mean it is estimating the volatility well, it is still far off even in that scenario.

Problem 2¶

Exercise 3A: Create intraday 5 minute returns¶

We work with the xts objects created in Problem 1. First, we aggregate the 1-minute prices to 5-minute frequency using the aggregateTS function. Then, we calculate intraday returns day-by-day using the makeReturns function, applying it separately for each trading day to avoid including overnight returns.

bac_5min  <- aggregateTS(bac_xts,  alignBy = "minutes", alignPeriod = 5, dropna = TRUE)
xom_5min  <- aggregateTS(xom_xts,  alignBy = "minutes", alignPeriod = 5, dropna = TRUE)

Exercise 4A: Create and compare RV created from prices and returns¶

We now compare the realized volatility from the manually calculated intraday 5min returns to those calculated automatically by the rCov function. If we calculated the RV correctly, we expect those differences to be 0 for all rows.

In [36]:
#calculate RV from prices with makeReturns=TRUE
RV_msft_5min <- rCov(rData = msft_5min, makeReturns = TRUE)
index(RV_msft_5min) <- as.Date(index(RV_msft_5min))

Exercise 5: compare intraday RVs for periods¶

We now define the sub-periods for comparison using the same intervals as in Problem 1. Since we are working with 5-minute data, the last timestamp in each sub-period will be rounded down to the nearest 5-minute mark. For example, the sub-period ending at 9:29 will end at 9:25.

3.319415e-04 6.460959e-05 4.604977e-05 2.019909e-05 7.143786e-05

MSFT exhibits the lowest overall RV across all sub-periods, followed by BAC, with XOM showing the highest levels particularly in the pre-market window. For MSFT, this may reflect its extreme liquidity. Tight bid-ask spreads and deep order books mean individual trades do not move the price much. BAC's higher RV may stem from its exposure to macro uncertainty and interest rate movements, while XOM's elevated pre-market RV likely reflects large overnight movements in crude oil prices that get priced in at the open.

The three companies display quite different intraday variance profiles. For XOM, the 7:00-9:29 window dominates with RV dropping sharply afterwards, possibly due to overnight oil price adjustments being priced in at the open. BAC shows highest RV in the first two windows, perhaps reflecting sensitivity to macroeconomic releases typically published before or at market open, with only a modest after-hours pickup. MSFT displays a different pattern. The dominant spike occurs at 16:00-18:00, likely driven by earnings announcements and corporate events that technology companies typically release after market close.

The boxplot complements the total sum plot by showing the distribution of daily RV within each sub-period. This is important because the total sum tells us nothing about day-to-day variability. For all three companies, the distribution is highly right-skewed with a median near zero and numerous extreme outliers, particularly in the 7:00-9:29 and 16:00-18:00 windows. This suggests that elevated total RV in those windows is driven not by uniformly high variance every day, but by occasional extreme events such as earnings shocks, surprise macro releases, or geopolitical developments, while most days remain relatively calm.

Exercise 6B¶

Compared to the 1-minute results, the differences are smaller in magnitude. This is because with 5-minute data there are approximately 5 times fewer squared returns being summed per day, meaning fewer sequential arithmetic operations and thus less accumulated rounding error.

For all three companies, the 9:30-10:59 window accounts for the largest average share of daily RV, despite being only a 90-minute window. This is an important refinement of what we found in exercise 5. While the total sum plot suggested that the 7:00-9:29 window was more important for XOM and comparable for BAC, once we normalize for window length it becomes clear that 9:30-10:59 is the most variance-intensive period per unit of time for all three companies. This window captures the immediate aftermath of the NYSE open at 08:30 CT, where overnight information gets rapidly priced in.

The company-specific patterns from exercise 5 are still visible but appear more balanced here. For MSFT, the 16:00-18:00 window remains the second largest contributor, consistent with after-hours earnings releases concentrating variance in that period. For BAC, the 7:00-9:29 and 9:30-10:59 windows together account for roughly half of daily RV. For XOM, the distribution is somewhat more even across periods compared to the other two companies, with 7:00-9:29, 9:30-10:59, and 11:00-14:29 all contributing meaningfully, suggesting that oil price-driven variance is more spread throughout the day rather than concentrated at a single event.

The time series plots on the left show substantial day-to-day variation in these shares for all three companies, with individual sub-periods occasionally dominating up to 80-90% of daily RV. This confirms the conclusion from the boxplots in exercise 5 that the elevated average shares in certain windows are driven by occasional extreme events rather than consistently high variance every day.

Exercise 8A: repeat with prices instead of returns¶

In [51]:
# Helper function to safely calculate sub-period RV from prices
safe_rv <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) > 1) {
    xts(as.numeric(rCov(x, makeReturns = TRUE)), order.by = as.Date(index(x)[1]))
  } else if (nrow(x) == 1) {
    xts(0, order.by = as.Date(index(x)[1]))
  } else {
    NULL
  }
}

# 1. MSFT Prices (Using pre-calculated RV_msft_5min)
msft_combined_pr_5min <- RV_msft_5min
colnames(msft_combined_pr_5min) <- "Full_RV"
for (i in seq_along(intervals)) {
  sub_split <- split(na.omit(msft_5min[intervals[i]]), f = "days")
  daily_sub_rv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sub_split, safe_rv))
  colnames(daily_sub_rv) <- paste0("P", i)
  msft_combined_pr_5min <- merge(msft_combined_pr_5min, daily_sub_rv, join = "left")
}
msft_combined_pr_5min[is.na(msft_combined_pr_5min)] <- 0

cat("\n--- BAC Mean RV by Sub-period (Prices, 5-min) ---\n")
print(colMeans(bac_combined_pr_5min[, 2:6], na.rm = TRUE))

# XOM
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(7, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
plot(colSums(xom_combined_pr_5min[, 2:6], na.rm = TRUE), type = "b", col = "red", pch = 16, xaxt = "n",
     xlab = "", ylab = "Total Sum RV", main = "XOM: Intraday Volatility (Prices, 5-min)")
axis(1, at = 1:5, labels = labels, las = 2)
boxplot(as.data.frame(xom_combined_pr_5min[, 2:6]), names = labels, las = 2, main = "XOM: RV Dist (Prices, 5-min)")
cat("\n--- XOM Mean RV by Sub-period (Prices, 5-min) ---\n")
print(colMeans(xom_combined_pr_5min[, 2:6], na.rm = TRUE))
